subject.title: feat: add readiness conditions and providers

question: Should OpenClaw V1 commit to the public, activation-scoped `api.registerReadinessCriterion` contract and operator-selected `gateway.readiness` criteria, or should plugin registration be deferred while core-only readiness ships first?
rationale: This is not a mechanical repair: the new callback and selector identifiers become supported Plugin SDK and configuration contracts, with intentional fail-closed availability effects for operators who opt in.

options.title: Sponsor the public readiness seam
options.body: Accept the generic Plugin SDK registration and configuration identifiers as V1 contracts, then require exact-head fresh-install and upgrade evidence before merge.

options.title: Stage core readiness first
options.body: Keep canonical core conditions and the CLI/HTTP projection, but remove plugin registration and selection until a narrower public SDK contract has an owner-approved design.

options.title: Pause the feature
options.body: Defer readiness expansion if the repository does not currently want another public Gateway and Plugin SDK surface.

recommendation.title: Sponsor the public readiness seam
recommendation.body: Accept the generic Plugin SDK registration and configuration identifiers as V1 contracts, then require exact-head fresh-install and upgrade evidence before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main history shows direct ownership of the public Plugin SDK entrypoint and its boundary discipline.
